This is the consolidated reference for couch allergies: the causes, what cleaning can and can't fix, and when the couch itself has to go. Each answer links to the full guide where there's more to say.

## The Causes

### Why does my couch make me sneeze or itch?

Three usual suspects: dust-mite allergen accumulated in foam, pet dander and dried saliva worked into fabric, and mold from past moisture. Fabric couches collect all three because they're warm, humid from body contact, and stocked with skin cells. Contact itching specifically is covered in [why your couch makes you itch](/blog/home-cleaning/why-does-my-couch-make-me-itch/) and [sofa dermatitis](/blog/home-cleaning/what-is-sofa-dermatitis/).

### Can a couch cause allergies even if it looks clean?

Yes. The allergen load lives in foam and seams, not on the visible surface. Age, moisture history, and persistent symptoms matter more than appearance.

### Do dust mites bite?

No. The reaction is to proteins in their waste, not bites. Actual bite marks mean a different pest.

## Cleaning

### What kills dust mites in a couch?

Heat above about 130°F, humidity held below 50%, freezing, and HEPA vacuuming to remove the allergen residue. The full routine is in [removing dust mites step by step](/blog/home-cleaning/remove-dust-mites-from-your-couch-step-by-step/).

### How do I remove pet dander from a couch?

HEPA vacuuming, hot-washing anything removable, a washable cover on the pet's spot, and an air purifier near the couch. [Cleaning vs. replacing for pet allergies](/blog/home-cleaning/pet-allergies-and-couches-cleaning-vs-replacing/) covers the limits.

### Does steam cleaning help with allergies?

For fabric, yes. For foam, barely, and added moisture can create mold risk if the cushion doesn't dry fully. The complete method is in [how to remove allergens from a couch](/blog/home-cleaning/how-to-remove-allergens-from-couch/).

### Can a moldy couch be cleaned?

Surface mildew sometimes. Mold inside foam, no. [Moldy couch: clean or replace](/blog/home-cleaning/moldy-couch-removal-tips-when-to-replace/) explains how to tell which you have.

## Replacing

### What couch materials are best for allergies?

Leather, faux leather, and tight-weave microfiber. Worst are high-pile fabrics and anything with deep crevices. The full ranking is in [best and worst couch materials for allergies](/blog/home-cleaning/best-worst-couch-materials-for-allergies/).

### When should I replace a couch for allergy reasons?

When symptoms persist after a thorough deep clean, when the couch has moisture or mold history, when it's 7 to 10 years old with heavy use, or when an allergic household member is getting worse rather than stable. See [how long a couch should last](/blog/home-cleaning/how-long-should-a-couch-last/).

### How do I get rid of an allergy-causing couch?

[Removal starts at $90](/couch-removal/) with the carry-out included and same-day pickup in most cities before 2PM local time. Disclose mold or pests at booking. A couch with allergen issues but otherwise good condition may still qualify for [donation](/blog/eco-friendly-living/can-couch-be-donated/); one with odor or mold will not.
